h1. Deployment of Dependency Track Flow

This document describes how to deploy Dependency Track using Docker Compose, with secure authentication, HTTPS, and a production-ready reverse proxy.

h2. Overview

Dependency Track is deployed as a multi-container stack using Docker Compose. The setup includes:
* Dependency Track API server
* Dependency Track frontend
* Swagger UI and Swagger Editor for API documentation
* Caddy reverse proxy for unified HTTPS access
* Permanent storage for application data

h2. Key Features

* *Secure authentication* via LDAP/Active Directory (configurable)
* *HTTPS* enabled using Caddy reverse proxy (supports custom certificates)
* *Single-origin access* for all services (no CORS issues)
* *Permanent storage* for all Dependency Track data
* *Healthchecks* for all major services
* *Automatic image updates* with Docker Compose pull policy

h2. Directory Structure

|| Directory/File || Purpose ||
| docker-compose.yml | Main stack definition |
| Caddyfile | Caddy reverse proxy configuration |
| certs/ | Directory for SSL/TLS certificates and private keys |
| output/ | Reports and documentation |
| resources/scripts/ | Utility scripts |

h2. Caddy Reverse Proxy

Caddy is used as a reverse proxy to:
* Terminate HTTPS (using Let's Encrypt or custom certificates)
* Route all traffic to the correct service (API, frontend, Swagger)
* Enforce security headers

h3. Custom Certificates
To use your own certificate and private key, place them in the certs/ directory and reference them in the Caddyfile:

{code}
tls /certs/your-cert.cer /certs/your-key.key
{code}

h2. Environment Configuration

All non-secret configuration is managed via environment variables in the Docker Compose file. Secrets (such as admin passwords) are managed using Docker secrets and are not stored in version control.

h2. Healthchecks

Each service includes a healthcheck to ensure reliability and automatic restarts if a service becomes unhealthy.

h2. Keeping Images Up to Date

The stack uses the latest images for all services and sets the pull policy to always. To update all images, run:
{code}
docker compose pull
{code}

h2. Deployment Steps

h3. Step 1: Create External Volumes

{code:bash}
docker volume create dtrack_postgres_data
docker volume create dtrack_apiserver_data
docker volume create swagger
{code}

These volumes persist data across container restarts and upgrades.

h3. Step 2: Deploy the Stack

{code:bash}
docker compose up -d
{code}

h3. Step 3: Verify Deployment

{code:bash}
docker compose ps
{code}

All services should show as "running".

h2. Permanent Storage

All application data is stored in persistent volumes to ensure data is retained across restarts and upgrades.

h2. Accessing the Application

Once deployed, access the stack via HTTPS at your configured domain. All services (API, frontend, Swagger UI/Editor) are available under the same origin.

h2. Security Notes

* Only the Caddy container has access to SSL/TLS private keys.
* Secrets are never stored in version control.
* All services are isolated on a private Docker network.

h2. Troubleshooting

* Check service health with Docker Compose commands:
{code}
docker compose ps
{code}
* Review logs for any service:
{code}
docker compose logs <service>
{code}

h2. Encrypting and Decrypting Secrets

To safely commit your .env and secrets files to version control, use the provided script to encrypt or decrypt them with a password:

* To encrypt:
{code}
./resources/scripts/secret_encryptor.sh encrypt .env admin_password postgres_password
{code}
* To decrypt:
{code}
./resources/scripts/secret_encryptor.sh decrypt .env.enc admin_password.enc postgres_password.enc
{code}

You will be prompted for a password during both encryption and decryption. Choose a strong password and remember it—anyone with this password can decrypt the files, and without it, the files cannot be recovered. Do not share the password in the repository.

Only commit the .enc files to git, never the unencrypted secrets.
